# Giada, Font of Hope: Calling All Angels (upgraded)

- **Format:** Commander (100 cards)
- **Archetype:** Mono-white Angel tribal: a snowballing flying team with a lifegain sub-theme; midrange that goes wide in the air
- **Played by:** either. Suits whoever likes flyers and big lifegain turns, and it's the simpler of the two Commander precons (complexity 2).
- **Status:** idea
- **Target bracket:** 2 (Core)
- **Complexity:** 2/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys
- **Configuration:** **Commander** set (builds alongside Gisa and Finneas) and the **Commander-season** set (alongside Izzet, Gruul, Rabbits and Vampires).

Giada is a cheap 2-mana flying Angel who makes every Angel that enters after her bigger: each one enters with a +1/+1 counter for every Angel you already control, Angel tokens included. The deck floods the sky with Angels, gains heaps of life, turns that life into extra Angels and cards, and then wins by attacking in the air. It's straightforward, proactive and very visual, so it suits a player who likes building a big board and swinging with flyers. It stays at Bracket 2 because it has no Game Changers, no combos and no land destruction.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **1x Path to Exile** (replaces Exorcise). A 1-mana instant that exiles any creature (its controller may fetch a basic land). Exorcise is a sorcery that only hits creatures with power 4+ (or an artifact/enchantment). It's the biggest removal upgrade per dollar and is in 76% of Giada decks on EDHREC. Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices (A$4.00 on 2026-09-28), so there's no need to wait. The Finneas target list also wants one, so buy 2 if you build both. *Also useful in: 60-card Angels / Orzhov / Rabbits (a 4th Swords-class removal spell); Finneas Commander target list.*
2. **1x Folk Hero** (replaces Angelic Destiny). A 2-mana Background enchantment that you can play from the 99. While Giada is on the battlefield, the first Angel spell you cast each turn draws a card (your commander gains 'whenever you cast a spell that shares a creature type with this creature, draw a card', once each turn). That includes your opponents' turns, e.g. flashing in Sigarda's Vanguard. It's in 36% of Giada decks on EDHREC and is the best card-per-dollar buy on the list. Angelic Destiny is a 4-mana aura that costs you tempo when the creature is removed. Commander-only: it does nothing without a commander. *Also useful in: Finneas Commander (Finneas is a Rabbit Archer, so every Rabbit spell draws). Not Gisa (she's a Human Wizard, so Zombie spells don't share a type)..*
3. **1x Angel of Sanctions** (replaces Seraph of the Sword). A 3/4 flying Angel that can exile any nonland permanent an opponent controls until it leaves the battlefield, and can come back once as a token copy via embalm ({5}{W}). It's removal on a body that also adds to Giada's Angel count. It isn't on EDHREC's Giada page; it's picked here as a cheap removal creature. *Also useful in: 60-card Mono-W Angels (it's in that deck's Tier 2 list).*
4. **1x Angel of Invention** (replaces Vanguard Seraph). A flying, vigilance, lifelink Angel that gives every other creature you control +1/+1 (an anthem) and either makes two 1/1 Servos or gets two +1/+1 counters (fabricate 2). It raises the whole team's damage and feeds the lifegain payoffs. *Also useful in: 60-card Angels; Finneas (go-wide anthem).*
5. **1x Herald's Horn** (replaces Endless Atlas). Name Angel: Angel creature spells cost 1 less, and at each of your upkeeps you look at the top card and may take it into your hand if it's an Angel. 27 of the 99 cards are Angels, so that's roughly 1 upkeep in 4. It's cheaper and better card flow than Endless Atlas's {2}-per-card draw, and it's in 58% of Giada decks on EDHREC. Reprinted in Foundations Commander (FDC 2026, 2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: Any tribal Commander deck: Gisa (Zombie), Finneas (Rabbit).*
6. **1x Angelic Accord** (replaces Always Watching). At the beginning of each end step (yours and opponents'), if you gained 4+ life that turn, you create a 4/4 flying Angel. One Angel entering with Bishop of Wings out, a connecting Lyra attack, or Linden plus four white attackers all turn it on. The tokens are Angels, so they get Giada counters too. It's in 42% of Giada decks on EDHREC. *Also useful in: 60-card Angels; 60-card Vampires / lifegain decks.*
7. **1x Myriad Landscape** (replaces Plains). A land that later fetches two Plains ({2}, tap, sacrifice): ramp without using a spell slot, plus two landfall triggers for Emeria Shepherd, which can return permanents straight to the battlefield because they're Plains. The Gisa target list also wants one, so buy 2 in total. *Also useful in: Every Commander deck (the Gisa target list already includes it).*
8. **1x Valkyrie Harbinger** (replaces Merchant of Truth). A 4/5 flying lifelink Angel that creates a 4/4 flying, vigilance Angel at the beginning of each end step in which you gained 4+ life. Its own attack usually turns that on, so it's a top-end threat that makes more threats. It's in 65% of Giada decks on EDHREC. *Also useful in: 60-card Angels.*
9. **1x Sigarda's Vanguard** (replaces Herald of Eternal Dawn). A 5-mana flash flier. Whenever it enters or attacks, you choose any number of creatures with different powers, and they gain double strike until end of turn. Giada's uneven counters make most of your Angels different sizes. It's a telegraphed finisher, and it lowers the curve by replacing a 7-drop. *Also useful in: 60-card Angels (finisher).*
10. **1x Well of Lost Dreams** (replaces Tome of Legends). Turns lifegain into cards: whenever you gain life, you may pay {X}, up to the amount gained, and draw X. The deck gains life constantly (Bishop of Wings, Seraph Sanctuary, Righteous Valkyrie, Lyra, Linden), so it fixes mono-white's weak late-game card draw. It's mana-hungry, so it's best once you have 7+ mana. *Also useful in: 60-card Vampires / any lifegain deck.*

## Substitutes

The Owned-only version below plays these cards until the Tier-1 buys arrive. Every owned card is a reasonable Commander card, so the deck is fully playable once the precon arrives on 2 Oct.

| Buy (target list) | Owned card played until it arrives | What the swap costs |
|---|---|---|
| Path to Exile | Exorcise | **Medium.** Exorcise is sorcery-speed and only hits creatures with power 4+ (or an artifact/enchantment); Path answers any creature at instant speed for 1 mana |
| Folk Hero | Angelic Destiny | **Medium.** Destiny gives one creature +4/+4, flying and first strike, and returns to your hand if that creature dies. Folk Hero draws a card each turn you cast an Angel while Giada is out |
| Angel of Sanctions | Seraph of the Sword | **Medium.** You lose a removal spell attached to a flier; Seraph is only a hard-to-kill attacker |
| Angel of Invention | Vanguard Seraph | **Medium.** No team-wide +1/+1 and no lifelink |
| Herald's Horn | Endless Atlas | **Small–medium.** Atlas still draws a card for {2} a turn, but Angels don't get cheaper and there are no free Angels off the top |
| Angelic Accord | Always Watching | **Medium.** Always Watching is a decent anthem (nontoken creatures +1/+1 and vigilance), but Accord makes a 4/4 flier most turns |
| Myriad Landscape | Plains | **Small.** One less ramp effect |
| Valkyrie Harbinger | Merchant of Truth | **Medium.** Merchant is a 2/5 flier that makes Clues when your nontoken creatures die; Harbinger is a lifelink threat that makes 4/4 Angels |
| Sigarda's Vanguard | Herald of Eternal Dawn | **Small.** Herald (7 mana, flash, 'you can't lose') is a safety net rather than a finisher; the curve is a bit higher |
| Well of Lost Dreams | Tome of Legends | **Small–medium.** Tome draws about 1 card a turn for {1} while Giada attacks; Well turns big lifegain turns into several cards |

**Changes from the precon to the owned list (12 in, 12 out, all free pool cards):**
- **In:** Generous Gift, Stroke of Midnight, Stasis Snare, Prayer of Binding (flexible removal); Burnished Hart, Wayfarer's Bauble (ramp); Mazemind Tome (draw); Adaptive Automaton (Angel lord); Linden, the Steadfast Queen (lifegain engine); Divine Resilience, Make a Stand (board-wipe protection); Rogue's Passage.
- **Out:** Reya Dawnbringer (9 mana), Day of Judgment (a third wipe in a creature deck), Defy Death, Cut a Deal, Secret Rendezvous, Destroy Evil, Invoke the Divine, Search the Premises, Segovian Angel, Speaker of the Heavens, Temple of the False God, Radiant Fountain.
- Keep the cut cards in the deck box as a 'maybe pile': swap in Invoke the Divine or Destroy Evil if a table is full of artifacts and enchantments.

## Notes

### Game plan in plain words

**Commander basics:**
- Everyone starts on 40 life.
- Giada starts in the *command zone*, a spot beside your deck, and you can cast her from there any time you could cast a creature.
- If she dies or is exiled, you can put her back in the command zone. Each recast costs {2} more than the last (the *commander tax*).

**The plan:**
1. **Turn 2: cast Giada.** She's a 2/2 flier with vigilance, so attacking doesn't tap her. She also taps for {W} that can only be spent on Angel spells, a bit of *ramp* (extra mana).
2. **Turns 3–5: make mana and play Angels.** *Mana rocks* (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Mind Stone and the Banners) are artifacts that tap for mana.
   - Giada's bonus: each new Angel enters with one +1/+1 counter for every Angel you already control. Giada counts, and so do Angel tokens.
   - So the 2nd Angel gets +1, the 3rd +2, the 4th +3, and your team snowballs.
3. **Gain lots of life.** Bishop of Wings (4 life per Angel), Seraph Sanctuary, Righteous Valkyrie, Lyra's lifelink and Linden all do this.
   - Life turns on your payoffs. Righteous Valkyrie gives your team +2/+2 once you're at 47 or more (starting life + 7). Angel of Vitality is +2/+2 at 25 or more, which is almost always.
   - In the target list, Angelic Accord and Valkyrie Harbinger turn 4+ life in a turn into a free 4/4 Angel, and Well of Lost Dreams turns life into cards.
4. **Win in the air.** Most opponents can't block flyers well. Attack the player who is most dangerous or least able to block, not always the same person.
5. **Removal is for real threats.** You have about 11 answers (Swords, Fateful Absence, Generous Gift, Stroke of Midnight, Grasp of Fate, Stasis Snare, Prayer of Binding, and so on). Save them for things that threaten to win or that stop your flyers.
6. **Board wipes are emergency buttons.** A *board wipe* is a spell that destroys lots of creatures. Austere Command and Cleansing Nova are for when you are clearly behind.
   - Austere Command lets you choose two of: all artifacts, all enchantments, all creatures with mana value 3 or less, all creatures with mana value 4 or more. It goes by *mana value* (the printed cost), not size. Giada's counters don't save a cheap Angel, and tokens have mana value 0, so the '3 or less' mode also kills your Angel and Spirit tokens.
   - **Make your own wipe one-sided:** cast the wipe, and while it's still on the stack cast Divine Resilience with kicker or Make a Stand. Your creatures survive and theirs don't.

### A good opening hand, and when to mulligan

- **Keep:** 3–5 lands plus something to do on turns 2–3. Giada is always available on turn 2, so a mana rock or a cheap Angel is ideal.
- **Also keep:** 2 lands plus a ramp piece (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Mind Stone, Marble Diamond, Wayfarer's Bauble, a Banner, Commander's Sphere, Starnheim Aspirant, or Herald's Horn in the target list) plus cheap plays.
- **Mulligan** (shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken):
  - 0–1 lands
  - 6–7 lands
  - a hand of only 6- and 7-drops with no ramp
- In multiplayer your first mulligan is free (Comprehensive Rules 103.5c): draw a new 7 and keep all of them; after that each mulligan puts one card on the bottom.
- About 69–70% of 7-card hands pass these rules (a simulation of 200,000 random hands from each list). About 29% of hands have exactly 2 lands, so the 2-land rule matters.

### Play tips

1. **Name Angel whenever a card asks for a creature type:** Vanquisher's Banner (draws a card every time you cast an Angel), Patchwork Banner, Metallic Mimic, Adaptive Automaton, and Herald's Horn in the target list. For Heraldic Banner, name **white**.
   - Metallic Mimic and Adaptive Automaton also get Giada's counters when you choose Angel. You apply their 'choose a type' effect first, so they enter as Angels (Comprehensive Rules 614.12 and 616.1).
2. **Order your Angels:** cheap Angels first, so your big ones (Lyra, Linvala, Sephara) arrive later with more counters. Sephara can also be cast for just {W} by tapping four untapped creatures with flying. Do it in your second main phase, using flyers that have vigilance or didn't attack.
3. **Sunblast Angel destroys every creature that is *tapped* when its enter ability resolves, yours too.**
   - Best time: your first main phase, before you attack. Opponents' creatures that attacked on their turns are still tapped, and yours untapped at the start of your turn.
   - **Don't tap Giada (or any other creature) for mana or an ability to help pay for it.** She'll still be tapped when the ability resolves and will die with the rest.
   - If you cast it after combat, only your untapped creatures survive: Giada and other vigilance flyers (Serra Avenger, Wojek Investigator, Metropolis Reformer), all your nontoken creatures while Thraben Watcher or Always Watching is out, and every creature you control while Angelic Field Marshal and Giada are both out.
4. **Court of Grace makes you the *monarch* when it enters:** you draw an extra card at each of your end steps. At each of your upkeeps it makes a 4/4 flying Angel if you're the monarch, or a 1/1 flying Spirit if you aren't. If an opponent's creature deals combat damage to you, its controller takes the crown, so keep a blocker home. While Archangel of Tithes is untapped, attacking you costs {1} per creature.
5. **Norn's Choirmaster:** every time Giada attacks (or is cast again), you *proliferate*: you can give each of your creatures that has +1/+1 counters one more.
6. **Folk Hero (target list):** keep Giada on the battlefield. The first Angel you cast each turn draws a card, and that works on opponents' turns too (for example, Sigarda's Vanguard has flash).
7. **Don't over-commit.**
   - If you already have a strong board, hold one or two creatures in hand so a board wipe doesn't wipe you out.
   - Save Divine Resilience (kicked, it protects your whole team) or Make a Stand for when someone casts 'destroy all creatures'. Cast it *in response*, before the wipe resolves.
   - Indestructible doesn't help against exile, 'sacrifice' or -X/-X effects.

### Watch out for

- **Board wipes:** Wrath of God, Damnation, Blasphemous Act, Toxic Deluge, Austere Command.
- **Shrink effects:** Massacre Wurm (in the Gisa deck) gives your creatures -2/-2 until end of turn. That kills small Angels without counters even through indestructible, and you lose 2 life for each creature of yours that dies.
- **Flyer hate:**
  - Reach creatures, and Hurricane-style damage to flyers.
  - Flying deathtouch blockers such as Vampire Nighthawk, which is common in Commander and in black 60-card decks. *Deathtouch* means any damage kills.
- **Sacrifice effects** ('each opponent sacrifices a creature', e.g. Fleshbag Marauder): keep a cheap creature or token around to sacrifice instead of Lyra.
- **Against Gisa's Zombies:**
  - They go wide on the ground and come back from the graveyard.
  - Angel of Finality exiles their graveyard.
  - Archangel of Tithes taxes their swarm.
  - Your flyers ignore their ground blockers.
- **Against stronger opponents:** expect stronger removal and counterspells. Spread your threats out rather than putting everything on one creature. Angelic Destiny (owned list) on Giada is tempting, but it's exactly what removal punishes.

### Commander-only notes

- Arcane Signet, Commander's Sphere, Tome of Legends (owned list), Angelic Field Marshal (lieutenant), Norn's Choirmaster and Folk Hero (target list) only work fully with a commander on the battlefield or in the command zone.
- That's fine here. Just don't move them into a 60-card deck expecting the same value.

**Cheap sidegrades (under A$1.30 est):** Serra Paragon (0.77; a 4-mana 3/4 Angel that replays a land or a ≤3-mana permanent from your graveyard each turn), Patron of the Valiant (0.14; puts a counter on every creature that already has a +1/+1 counter, which is every Giada Angel), Boon-Bringer Valkyrie (0.64), Resplendent Marshal (1.27; a 3/3 flier for Metropolis Reformer, but it needs an Angel card in your graveyard to do anything), Banishing Light (0.16; the cheapest printing is The List, which AU shops often don't stock), Archaeomancer's Map (1.12), Castle Ardenvale (0.36) or Path of Ancestry (0.30) for a Plains. Path of Ancestry is reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait.

**Optional sidegrade for Make a Stand:** Unbreakable Formation (0.97 est; out of stock at MTGMate on 2026-09-28). Cast in your own main phase, it also gives each of your creatures a +1/+1 counter and vigilance. Make a Stand already does the job of saving your team from a wipe, so this is only a small upgrade.

**Do NOT add (Game Changers → Bracket 3):** Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Protection, Farewell, Enlightened Tutor, Serra's Sanctum, The One Ring, Ancient Tomb. They all show up on EDHREC's Giada page. Re-check the list after the 12 Oct 2026 B&R announcement.

**Legal but a poor fit for a social table:** Serra's Emissary (A$6.49 est; reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander, 2 Oct 2026). Naming 'creature' gives you and your creatures protection from creatures, which shuts creature decks out of the game. Karmic Guide is also left out on purpose: it's a common piece of reanimation loops.
